case_title: Modinsab Kasimsab Kanchagar v. State of Karnataka & Anr.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B, s.498-A; Dowry Prohibition Act s.3, s.4, s.6
aggravating_circumstances: Demand for property or valuable security, harassment leading to suicide
offence_finally_established: Section 498-A IPC and Sections 3, 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act
neutral_facts: The accused, a man, married a woman who later committed suicide. The prosecution alleged that the accused harassed the deceased for a demand of Rs. 10,000/- which was for repayment of a society loan. The deceased's family was unable to meet the demand, and the deceased committed suicide after being harassed by the accused. The trial court acquitted the accused, but the High Court convicted him for the offences under Section 498-A IPC and Sections 3, 4, and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act. The accused was sentenced to approximately two years of imprisonment for the offence under Section 498-A IPC and six months for each of the offences under the Dowry Prohibition Act.
